title: lightpanda-io /browser
summary:
Lightpanda Browser The headless browser built from scratch for AI agents and automation. Not a Chromium fork. Not a WebKit patch. A new browser, written in Zig. 16x lighter and 9x faster than Chromium. Benchmarks Requesting 933 real web pages over the network on a AWS EC2 m5.large instance.
See benchmark details . Metric Lightpanda Headless Chrome Difference Memory (peak, 100 pages) 123MB 2GB ~16x less Execution time (100 pages) 5s 46s ~9x faster Quick start Install Package Managers Latest nightly from Homebrew: brew install lightpanda-io/browser/lightpanda Latest nightly from Arch Linux User Repository: yay -S lightpanda-nightly-bin Download from the nightly builds You can download the last binary from the nightly
builds for
Linux and MacOS for both x86_64 and aarch64. For Linux curl -L -o lightpanda https://github.com/lightpanda-io/browser/releases/download/nightly/lightpanda-x86_64-linux && \ chmod a+x ./lightpanda Verify the binary before running anything: ./lightpanda version Linux aarch64 is also available If you use Nix , you can run Lightpanda directly from the flake without downloading a binary: nix run github:lightpanda-io/browser -- --help Or pin it as an input in your own flake: { inputs . lightpanda . url = "github:lightpanda-io/browser" ; } Note: The Linux release binaries are linked against glibc. On musl-based Linux distributions (Alpine, etc.) the binary fails with cannot execute: required file not found because the glibc dynamic linker is missing. Use a glibc-based base image: the current release binaries need glibc 2.35 ( x86_64 ) or 2.38 ( arm64 ), so debian:bookworm-slim (2.36) is fine on x86_64 but too old for arm64 — use FROM ubuntu:24.04 , FROM debian:trixie-slim , or FROM debian:forky-slim there — or build from sources . Android / Termux: there is no native Android build. bajada: Lightpanda lanzó un navegador headless escrito en Zig diseñado específicamente para agentes IA y automatización, con 16x menos memoria y 9x más velocidad que Chromium. Es open-source y promete ser alternativa eficiente para automatización web con IA.
bajada_en: Lightpanda released a headless browser written in Zig designed specifically for AI agents and automation, using 16x less memory and running 9x faster than Chromium. It's open-source and promises to be an efficient alternative for web automation with AI.

title: LSREP: A Longitudinal State-Replay Protocol for Evaluating Conversational Memory [R]
summary: I'm an undergraduate researcher working independently on conversational memory systems. I developed LSREP to evaluate how persistent memory accumulates, changes and retrieves information over the course of an evolving conversation.Instead of relying only on isolated endpoint questions, LSREP combines chronological replay, lifecycle schedules, repeated probes, evolving reference answers and mechanism-fidelity checks.The accompanying architectural case study is ICE v2, a local-first conversational memory system.The evaluation covers 1,985 turns, 219 distinct probes and 1,211 probe-checkpoint observations across 52 checkpoints, using a private single-user history.An important part of the findings is that ICE v2 didnotoutperform pure vector-RAG on the matched LongMemEval evaluation. The ordinary-density replay results also did not establish a quality advantage. The paper discusses the limitations and mechanism-fidelity findings rather than treating the architecture as validated in its entirety.I'm particularly interested in feedback on the evaluation methodology: what else should a longitudinal memory benchmark test to distinguish successful recall from reliable maintenance of evolving conversational state?Paper:https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16730Code and evaluation artifacts:https://github.com/Deepnar/iceFrozen software artifact:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21759702This is an arXiv preprint and an ongoing independent research project.(I couldn't find anything about the tag in the title in the rules, so i assumed [R] for research, if its wrong please inform)submitted by/u/Deepnar_S[link][comments]
title_es: LSREP: protocolo para evaluar memoria conversacional persistente
bajada: Un investigador desarrolló LSREP, un protocolo de evaluación para sistemas de memoria conversacional que mide cómo la IA acumula, modifica y recupera información en conversaciones prolongadas. El método es más riguroso que benchmarks tradicionales para memoria persistente.
bajada_en: A researcher developed LSREP, an evaluation protocol for conversational memory systems that measures how AI accumulates, modifies, and retrieves information in long conversations. The method is more rigorous than traditional persistent memory benchmarks.

title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights [R]
summary: Link:https://rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming/Snippet: “We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good atnatively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms. This might be a big deal for both optimization and interpretability.Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astracan tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, ithas no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networksthat outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.”Very surprising result, I didn’t expect frontier models to have this capability that has not been optimized for, and it’s something humans cannot do either.submitted by/u/RobbinDeBank[link][comments]
title_es: LLMs pueden leer y escribir pesos de redes neuronales nativamente
bajada: Research muestra que LLMs frontier pueden natively leer y escribir pesos de redes neuronales sin optimización previa, superando capacidades humanas. Tiene implicaciones mayores para optimización e interpretabilidad de modelos.
bajada_en: Research shows frontier LLMs can natively read and write neural network weights without prior optimization, surpassing human capabilities. Major implications for model optimization and interpretability.

bajada_en: MIT Tech Review reports AI agents consume 10-50x more tokens than basic chat prompts while planning, coding, testing, and iterating. Critical for understanding true costs of agentic deployments.
